_meta.indication: HEMLIBRA is indicated for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients with hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency) with factor VIII inhibitors.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, open-label Phase 3 study comparing prophylactic emicizumab (Arm A) versus no prophylaxis (Arm B) at a 2:1 randomization ratio, with two additional nonrandomized arms.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and adolescent patients (≥12 years old) with hemophilia A with FVIII inhibitors who received episodic treatment with bypassing agents prior to study entry.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Number of treated bleeds over the efficacy period (Arm A emicizumab prophylaxis vs. Arm B no prophylaxis).
pivotal_trials.n: 53 randomized (Arm A N=35; Arm B N=18); plus non-randomized Arm C N=49 and Arm D N=7.
pivotal_trials.result: Model-based ABR 2.9 (95% CI 1.7, 5.0) with emicizumab vs. 23.3 (12.3, 43.9) with no prophylaxis; ABR ratio 0.13 (95% CI 0.057, 0.277), p<0.0001 — an 87% reduction in treated bleeds.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were injection site reactions (19%), headache (15%), and arthralgia (10%). Boxed warning for thrombotic microangiopathy and thromboembolism with concurrent aPCC use: TMA reported in 1.6% (3/189) and thrombotic events in 1.1% (2/189).
target_moa: Emicizumab is a humanized monoclonal modified IgG4 bispecific antibody that bridges activated factor IX (FIXa) and factor X to restore the function of missing activated factor VIII needed for effective hemostasis, functioning even in the presence of FVIII inhibitors.

boxed_warning.content: Thrombotic microangiopathy and thromboembolism: cases were reported when on average a cumulative amount of >100 U/kg/24 hours of aPCC was administered for 24 hours or more to patients receiving HEMLIBRA prophylaxis. Monitor and discontinue aPCC and suspend HEMLIBRA if symptoms occur.

rems.type: No REMS required; risks can be managed through labeling and a Medication Guide. No additional risk management strategies were assessed to be necessary beyond the recommended labeling.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not presented to an advisory committee.

summary.text: HEMLIBRA (emicizumab-kxwh) received a Priority review as an original BLA. It was granted orphan designation for hemophilia A (1/10/2014) and breakthrough therapy designation (9/2/2015) for patients with hemophilia A with FVIII inhibitors. Full (not accelerated) approval was based on the reduction in annualized bleeding rate demonstrated in Study HAVEN1.

The recommendation is based on the finding of a decrease in annualized bleeding rate (ABR) with emicizumab prophylaxis compared with no prophylaxis demonstrated in Study HAVEN1.
